desc:
A text editor holds a sequence of items (think of characters, each an integer) and a cursor that sits between two items, or at either end. The editor starts empty with the cursor at the beginning. Each operation is a pair [type, x]:

  • [0, x]: insert the item x exactly at the cursor; the cursor ends up right after it. Nothing is reported.
  • [1, k]: delete up to k items immediately before the cursor (fewer if there are fewer). Report how many items were deleted.
  • [2, k]: move the cursor left by up to k items (stopping at the beginning). Report the sum of the up to 10 items immediately before the cursor after the move (0 if there are none).
  • [3, k]: move the cursor right by up to k items (stopping at the end). Report the same sum as for type 2.

Return the reported numbers in the order of the operations. For example ops = [[0,5],[0,6],[0,7],[2,1],[0,9],[1,2],[3,5]] gives [11, 2, 12]. The items become 5 6 7 with the cursor at the end; moving left one place leaves 5 6 | 7 (sum before the cursor 5+6 = 11), item 9 is inserted giving 5 6 9 | 7, deleting two items before the cursor removes 6 and 9 (report 2, leaving 5 | 7) and moving right by 5 stops at the end (sum 5+7 = 12).
constraints: For an insert, -10<sup>8</sup> ≤ x ≤ 10<sup>8</sup>; for the other types, 0 ≤ k ≤ 10,000
The answer contains one number per operation of type 1, 2 or 3
hints: Every operation happens at the cursor. Think of the text as two parts: everything left of the cursor and everything right of it.

Keep the left part as a stack whose top is the item just before the cursor, and the right part as a stack whose top is the item just after the cursor. Insert and delete are pushes and pops on the left stack.

Moving the cursor by m = min(k, size) places means popping m items from one stack and pushing them onto the other. After a move, the sum of the last 10 items of the left stack is the number to report. (A doubly linked list with a cursor node does the same job.)
editorial: A doubly linked list with a cursor pointer is the textbook model: insert and delete next to the cursor are O(1) and moving costs one step per item. Two stacks give the same behaviour with simpler code. left holds the items before the cursor (top = nearest to the cursor) and right the items after it (top = nearest). Insert is left.append(x); delete pops up to k items from left; moving left transfers items from the top of left to right, moving right transfers the other way.

A move transfers at most min(k, size) items, so the cost of an operation is proportional to the distance the cursor really moves. Reporting the sum of the last 10 items of left costs O(10). Overall O(total cursor movement + q) time, which is at most O(q · n) and fast for these limits.
